24namespace superdex {
25/** @brief Linear solver types. */
26enum struct LinearSolverType {
27 /**
28 * @brief Conjugate Gradient (CG) solver.
29 *
30 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite systems.
31 * @note Unlike @ref LinearSolverType::ParallelCG, only matrix-vector products are parallelized.
32 * CG orthogonalization and preconditioner solves are not.
33 */
34 CG,
35
36 /** @brief Generalized Minimal Residual (GMRES) solver. */
37 GMRES,
38
39 /**
40 * @brief CUDA CG solver.
41 *
42 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite systems.
43 * @note Requires building with CUDA and a preconditioner with CUDA support.
44 *
45 * @see PreconditionerType
46 */
47 CudaCG,
48
49 /**
50 * @brief CUDA GMRES solver.
51 *
52 * @note Requires building with CUDA and a preconditioner with CUDA support.
53 *
54 * @see PreconditionerType
55 */
56 CudaGMRES,
57
58 /**
59 * @brief [Experimental] Augmented CG solver with Krylov subspace recycling.
60 *
61 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
62 * your own risk.
63 *
64 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite systems.
65 * @note Requires building with Eigen.
66 */
67 AugmentedCG,
68
69 /**
70 * @brief Direct solver based on the LDLt factorization without pivoting.
71 *
72 * @note Only valid for symmetric systems.
73 * @note May be unstable for indefinite or ill-conditioned systems.
74 * @note Uses a dense or a sparse factorization depending on the size and sparsity of the system.
75 */
76 LDLT,
77
78 /**
79 * @brief Direct solver based on the dense LU factorization without pivoting.
80 *
81 * @note May be unstable for ill-conditioned systems.
82 * @note The cost of the factorization is O(n^3). Will be slow for large systems.
83 * @note Consider using @ref LinearSolverType::LDLT if the system is symmetric.
84 */
85 LU,
86
87 /**
88 * @brief [Experimental] Asynchronous CG solver.
89 *
90 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
91 * your own risk.
92 *
93 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite systems.
94 * @note Async CG is a reformulation of the classical CG algorithm to compute the matrix-vector
95 * products in parallel to the orthogonalization and convergence check.
96 * @note Equivalent to the classical CG algorithm in exact-precision arithmetic, but has inferior
97 * stability properties in finite-precision arithmetic.
98 */
99 AsyncCG,
100
101 /**
102 * @brief [Experimental] Parallel CG solver.
103 *
104 * @warning Not deterministic.
105 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
106 * your own risk.
107 *
108 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite systems.
109 * @note Unlike @ref LinearSolverType::CG, all operations (matrix-vector products, preconditioner
110 * solves, CG orthogonalization) are parallelized.
111 * @note Requires a preconditioner with a parallel solve.
112 */
113 ParallelCG,
114
115 /**
116 * @brief Minimal Residual (MINRES) solver.
117 *
118 * @note Only valid for symmetric systems.
119 */
120 MINRES,
121
122 /**
123 * @brief [Experimental] CUDA sparse Cholesky factorization.
124 *
125 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
126 * your own risk.
127 *
128 * @note Only valid for sparse or block-sparse symmetric positive-definite systems.
129 * @note Requires building with CUDA.
130 */
131 ExperimentalCudaSparseCholesky,
132
133 /**
134 * @brief [Experimental] CUDA sparse LDLt factorization.
135 *
136 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
137 * your own risk.
138 *
139 * @note Only valid for sparse or block-sparse symmetric systems.
140 * @note Requires building with CUDA and cuDSS.
141 */
142 ExperimentalCudaSparseLDLT,
143
144 /**
145 * @brief [Experimental] CUDA sparse LU factorization.
146 *
147 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
148 * your own risk.
149 *
150 * @note Only valid for sparse or block-sparse systems.
151 * @note Requires building with CUDA.
152 */
153 ExperimentalCudaSparseLU,
154
155 /** @brief Let Mochi select the solver type based on the problem. */
156 Auto,
157
158 /** @brief Number of solver type enum values. */
159 Count,
160
161 /** @brief Default solver type. */
162 Default = Auto
163};
164} // namespace superdex

184namespace superdex {
185/**
186 * @brief Preconditioner types for the linear solver.
187 *
188 * @note Only used for iterative solvers.
189 * @note CUDA iterative solvers only support @ref PreconditionerType::None, @ref
190 * PreconditionerType::Jacobi and @ref PreconditionerType::BlockJacobi preconditioners.
191 */
192enum struct PreconditionerType {
193 /** @brief No preconditioner. */
194 None,
195
196 /**
197 * @brief Jacobi preconditioner.
198 *
199 * @note Only valid for matrices with non-zero diagonal entries.
200 */
201 Jacobi,
202
203 /**
204 * @brief Block Jacobi preconditioner with block size of 3.
205 *
206 * @note Only valid for matrices whose size is a multiple of 3 and whose 3x3 diagonal blocks are
207 * non-singular.
208 */
209 BlockJacobi,
210
211 /**
212 * @brief Symmetric successive over-relaxation (SSOR) preconditioner.
213 *
214 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite matrices.
215 */
216 SSOR,
217
218 /**
219 * @brief Block symmetric successive over-relaxation (SSOR) preconditioner with block size of 3.
220 *
221 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite matrices whose size is a multiple of 3 and
222 * whose 3x3 diagonal blocks are non-singular.
223 */
224 BlockSSOR,
225
226 /**
227 * @brief Dense LU factorization without pivoting.
228 *
229 * @note May be unstable for ill-conditioned matrices.
230 * @note The iterative solver should converge in 1 iteration.
231 */
232 LU,
233
234 /**
235 * @brief Algebraic multigrid (AMG).
236 *
237 * @note Only valid for 3x3 block sparse symmetric positive-definite matrices with non-singular
238 * 3x3 diagonal blocks.
239 */
240 AMG,
241
242 /**
243 * @brief Symmetric inverse preconditioner based on the dense LDLt factorization without pivoting.
244 *
245 * @note Only valid for symmetric matrices.
246 * @note May be unstable for indefinite or ill-conditioned matrices.
247 * @note The iterative solver should converge in 1 iteration.
248 */
249 SymInverse,
250
251 /**
252 * @brief Dense LDLt factorization without pivoting.
253 *
254 * @note Only valid for symmetric matrices.
255 * @note May be unstable for indefinite or ill-conditioned matrices.
256 * @note The iterative solver should converge in 1 iteration.
257 */
258 LDLT,
259
260 /** @brief Incomplete LU factorization with zero fill-in. */
261 ILU0,
262
263 /**
264 * @brief Incomplete Cholesky factorization with zero fill-in.
265 *
266 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite matrices.
267 */
268 IC0,
269
270 /**
271 * @brief Domain decomposition preconditioner, where each actor is a subdomain.
272 *
273 * @note By default, an appropriate preconditioner type is selected for each actor.
274 */
275 PerActor,
276
277 /**
278 * @brief [Experimental] Colored symmetric successive over-relaxation (SSOR) preconditioner.
279 *
280 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
281 * your own risk.
282 *
283 * @note Only valid for symmetric positive-definite matrices.
284 */
285 ColoredSSOR,
286
287 /**
288 * @brief [Experimental] @ref PreconditionerType::PerActor preconditioner that can switch the
289 * preconditioner type of each actor during the simulation to speed up the linear solves.
290 *
291 * @warning Some scenes can run slower than with @ref PreconditionerType::PerActor, and some steps
292 * can take longer than usual, causing latency spikes.
293 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
294 * your own risk.
295 */
296 AdaptivePerActor,
297
298 /** @brief Number of preconditioner type enum values. */
299 Count,
300
301 /** @brief Default preconditioner type. */
302 Default = PerActor
303};
304} // namespace superdex

324namespace superdex {
325/**
326 * @brief Norm types for the stopping criteria of the linear solver.
327 *
328 * @note @ref LinearSolverType::CG, @ref LinearSolverType::ParallelCG and @ref
329 * LinearSolverType::AsyncCG support every norm. @ref LinearSolverType::CudaCG supports every norm
330 * except @ref LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::ResidualPerActorWeighted, for which it uses @ref
331 * LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::PreconditionedResidualL2. @ref LinearSolverType::GMRES, @ref
332 * LinearSolverType::CudaGMRES, and @ref LinearSolverType::AugmentedCG always use the L2-norm of the
333 * residual regardless of this setting. @ref LinearSolverType::MINRES always uses the
334 * preconditioner-induced norm of the residual. Direct solvers do not have stop criteria.
335 */
336enum struct LinearSolverConvergenceNorm {
337 ResidualL2, ///< L2-norm of the residual: \f$\|r\|_2\f$.
338 PreconditionedResidualL2, ///< L2-norm of the preconditioned residual: \f$\|z\|_2\f$ where
339 ///< \f$z = M^{-1}r\f$.
340 ResidualPreconditionerInduced, ///< Preconditioner-induced norm of the residual:
341 ///< \f$\sqrt{\langle r, z \rangle}\f$ where \f$z = M^{-1}r\f$.
342 /**
343 * @brief Per-actor weighted L2-norm of the residual, each actor normalized by its own non-linear
344 * residual, so actors have comparable influence regardless of the magnitude of their residuals.
345 *
346 * @details \f$\|r\| = \sqrt{\sum_a \|r_a\|_W^2 / s_a^2}\f$, where
347 * \f$\|r_a\|_W = \sqrt{\sum_i w_i r_i^2}\f$ uses actor \f$a\f$'s weights from @ref
348 * NonLinearSolverConvergenceMode::PerActorWeighted, and \f$s_a\f$ is the larger of actor
349 * \f$a\f$'s non-linear residual in that norm and @ref NonLinearSolverParams::absTol, or, if both
350 * are zero, the largest actor's residual.
351 *
352 * @note In @ref NonLinearSolverConvergenceMode::Global mode, the solvers that support it use @ref
353 * LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::ResidualL2 instead.
354 */
355 ResidualPerActorWeighted,
356 Count, ///< Number of linear solver convergence norm enum values.
357 Default = PreconditionedResidualL2 ///< Default linear solver convergence norm.
358};
359} // namespace superdex
360
361MOCHI_ENUM_BEGIN(superdex::LinearSolverConvergenceNorm)
362MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(ResidualL2)
363MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(PreconditionedResidualL2)
364MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(ResidualPreconditionerInduced)
365MOCHI_ENUM_ITEM(ResidualPerActorWeighted)
366MOCHI_ENUM_COUNT(Count)
367MOCHI_ENUM_END()

371/** @brief Sentinel value for @ref LinearSolverParams::maxIter that lets Mochi automatically select
372 * the maximum number of linear solver iterations. */
373constexpr int kAutoLinearSolverMaxIter = -1;
374
375/** @brief Parameters for the linear solve performed in each iteration of the non-linear solver. */
376struct LinearSolverParams {
377 /** @brief Linear solver type. */
378 LinearSolverType solverType = LinearSolverType::Default;
379
380 /**
381 * @brief Preconditioner type.
382 *
383 * @note Applies only to iterative solvers.
384 */
385 PreconditionerType preconditionerType = PreconditionerType::Default;
386
387 /**
388 * @brief Norm used for the stopping criteria.
389 *
390 * @note Applies only to the solvers documented in @ref LinearSolverConvergenceNorm.
391 */
392 LinearSolverConvergenceNorm normType = LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::Default;
393
394 /**
395 * @brief Absolute residual norm tolerance for convergence.
396 *
397 * @note Applies only to iterative solvers.
398 * @note When the solver stops on @ref LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::ResidualPerActorWeighted, the
399 * absolute stop ends the solve only once every actor's weighted residual \f$\|r_a\|_W\f$ is at
400 * most @ref absTol. Otherwise, it bounds the solver's stopping norm.
401 * @note 0 leaves only the relative test.
402 * @note A negative value lets Mochi select it. When the solver stops on @ref
403 * LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::ResidualPerActorWeighted, Mochi selects 1% of the residual at
404 * which the non-linear solver accepts each actor: @ref NonLinearSolverParams::relTol times the
405 * actor's initial residual, or @ref NonLinearSolverParams::absTol if larger. When it stops on
406 * @ref LinearSolverConvergenceNorm::ResidualL2 in @ref NonLinearSolverConvergenceMode::Global
407 * mode, Mochi selects 1% of the residual at which the non-linear solver accepts the island.
408 * Otherwise, it selects 1e-9. The selection is 0 when @ref NonLinearSolverParams::absTol is 0 and
409 * either @ref NonLinearSolverParams::relTol or the initial residual of an actor or the island is
410 * 0, which leaves only the relative test.
411 */
412 real absTol = 1e-9_r;
413
414 /**
415 * @brief Relative residual norm tolerance for convergence, relative to the same norm of the
416 * right-hand side.
417 *
418 * @note Applies only to iterative solvers.
419 * @note Ignored when using @ref LinearToleranceStrategy::EisenstatWalker1 or @ref
420 * LinearToleranceStrategy::EisenstatWalker2 in the non-linear solver.
421 */
422 real relTol = 1e-5_r;
423
424 /**
425 * @brief Relative residual norm tolerance for divergence, relative to the same norm of the
426 * right-hand side.
427 *
428 * @note Applies only to iterative solvers.
429 */
430 real relDivTol = 1e10_r;
431
432 /**
433 * @brief Maximum number of iterations for iterative solvers.
434 *
435 * @note Applies only to iterative solvers.
436 * @note Must be positive or @ref kAutoLinearSolverMaxIter.
437 * @note @ref kAutoLinearSolverMaxIter lets Mochi select the maximum number of iterations based
438 * on the problem.
439 */
440 int maxIter = kAutoLinearSolverMaxIter;
441
442 /**
443 * @brief Krylov subspace dimension before restarting.
444 *
445 * @note Applies only to GMRES solvers (e.g., @ref LinearSolverType::GMRES, @ref
446 * LinearSolverType::CudaGMRES).
447 */
448 int restartSize = 1000;
449
450 /**
451 * @brief Abort solve if matrix is not SPD.
452 *
453 * @note Applies only to iterative SPD solvers (e.g., @ref LinearSolverType::CG, @ref
454 * LinearSolverType::CudaCG, @ref LinearSolverType::AugmentedCG).
455 */
456 bool abortIfNotSpd = false;
457
458 /** @brief Verbosity level for logging output. */
459 VerbosityLevel verbosity = VerbosityLevel::Warning;
460
461#if MOCHI_LANGUAGE_CPP20
462 bool operator==(LinearSolverParams const&) const = default;
463#endif
464
465 MOCHI_STRUCT_BEGIN(superdex::LinearSolverParams)
466 MOCHI_FIELD(solverType)
467 MOCHI_FIELD(preconditionerType)
468 MOCHI_FIELD(normType)
469 MOCHI_FIELD(absTol)
470 MOCHI_FIELD(relTol)
471 MOCHI_FIELD(relDivTol)
472 MOCHI_FIELD(maxIter)
473 MOCHI_FIELD(restartSize)
474 MOCHI_FIELD(abortIfNotSpd)
475 MOCHI_FIELD(verbosity)
476 MOCHI_STRUCT_END()
477};
478
